beta_new: From a crack behind a tree on the training wall's right side, ascend 25 feet to a stance near the Sherpa Connection tree, then continue upward beyond another tree, then via the evident break at the main wall's left.

moves.from: Protection up to 4 inches is adequate for leading.

beta_new: Start by a tree, or slightly left when the rock is damp, then go up along the leaning corner.

Start near the centre of the pristine white wall beneath a broken thin seam; work the seam to a horizontal crack beneath the first overhang, drift leftward and upward through the tiered overhangs passing a petite triangular beak, grab the bucket at the lip, and mantle onto easier ground.

moves.from: Take nuts, cams to 3 inches, plus a pair of small TCUs.

value.text: Nuts, cams to 3 in and two small TCUs.

beta_new: Begin by the big tree where the ramp starts on the left, and follow the prominent rightward-angling crack all the way up.

moves.from: nuts plus cams from small to medium suffice

value.text: Nuts plus cams from small to medium.

beta_new: Begin under an aged sleeve bolt, boulder up to the layback crack, and follow it.

Start at the roof sitting about face-high beside the big dihedral, gain the ledge above it by going in from the left, then follow cracks angling leftward before trending right to bolt one; delicate edging carries you by bolt two to a good layback hold.

Step onto a slim shelf and shuffle rightward to a lowering anchor that can't be seen from below; if toproping, slot a nut in to the anchor's left so the follower is spared a swing.
Starts from the top of the bouldering wall, with an exposed sidestep at Topaz, then crosses the ledge toward the corner's foot, which the final pitch ascends.

moves.from: take large nuts plus cams from small through medium

value.text: Large nuts plus cams from small to medium.

beta_new: Go directly upward on solid holds to the roof, step leftward, surmount it, and top out at the anchor.

Start up a gentle flared crack toward the roof block, undercling rightward beneath the roof to the flaring offwidth that reaches a ledge, then carry on over the face or move leftward toward the chain anchor above Intertwine.
Extend your placements with long slings, because the rope will drag badly as you go around the left side of the overhang.

moves.from: Extend your placements with long slings, because the rope will drag badly as you go around the left side of the overhang.

beta_new: Go up the short dihedral to the right of its neighbor, threading a sling in a drilled hole higher up for protection, then follow the bolted subtle arete above.
Climb to the first pocket, then go straight up to the double-carabiner anchor in the middle of the shelf above.
Descend the chimney from the belay ledge, then ascend the wall next to the easy groove, on its right. The funky basalt close to the top is where it gets hard.
Leave the approach gully and fight through an overhang to a finger crack, shift leftward, and take on a second crack above. It is a sustained fingers-and-forearms effort.
Begin as for the neighboring route, then veer left toward the anchors capping Jam and Jelly; various alternative boulder-style starts exist to the left.
Begin by clipping the bolts along the roof's right edge, then switch over to placing nuts for the remainder, which is unusual for a sport area.
It is the middle one among a trio of obvious cracks in the face and takes good gear if you place it well.
A pair of bolts beside the crack, on its west flank, take you to the chains above the chimney. A leaning tree bridges to the neighboring quarry-bolt buttress.

moves.from: A pair of bolts beside the crack

beta_new: Clip three bolts to reach a hueco, then continue through the left part of the upper corner.
Begin around fifteen feet beyond the crack on its right, work rightward and up to the first bolt, go straight to the second, then drift left to the anchors.
Enter either from the crack or by an optional face start slightly to its right, then continue across the lip to the anchors.
Begin on the arete's left side and wind upward to the anchors beneath the roof.
Follow the bolt line to the open hooks, and keep an eye out for wasps at the undercling.
Start about ten feet to the right of the neighboring route and clip four bolts as the line slants up and to the right.
Take the right part of the wall and place your gear in the small crack there.

Open with an awkward crack on the right wall to a small stance, then step into the chimney itself and squeeze upward with very little gear to a comfortable ledge with fixed anchors.

Strenuous moves lead back into the chimney for the final pitch, which you follow to the top.
Awkward, hard moves get you over the large roof and the wave feature, after which the line eases into thin, doubled left-facing corners that lead to the chains.
Use a stick-clip for the first bolt. Layback and edge up the leaning face for about 25 feet to the break, then pull through the scoop to reach the lip anchors.

Climb the face clipping two bolts, then a tense sequence gets you to bolt three. Next, traverse leftward beyond the final bolt into a crack that reaches the top. A dirtier runout alternative goes directly upward from bolt two.
Reach the Great White anchors first, then keep going with non-stop liebacks and underclings along the flake that leans left, clipping four bolts before the anchor.

Begin off a ramp that slants left, then work a string of buckets rightward to a cramped resting stance. More good holds continue rightward, passing under the large sloping roof; bolt number five is an awkward clip.
Layback and jam the steep finger crack until a pod gives a solid hand-jam rest. Then follow the thin hand crack rightward to a bolt, stretch for an unexpected hold, and finish on easier rock.

Pull up jugs from under the roofs, reach the largest roof and undercling out rightward. A white dike takes you up the wall above to a break; shift right a few feet and complete the climb in the open corner leading to the chains.

Go up the easy gully onto a ledge, then angle leftward over a horizontal break that takes a mid-sized or larger cam, arriving at the first bolt. The rest is steep, juggy rock that relaxes into a slab at the top.
Take the overhang directly below the old bolt, then continue on face holds up the wall above it.
Pass two bolts to reach a roof system that angles left, clip the bolt over the lip and pull through, then continue up the gently leaning headwall to anchors beneath another roof.

Begin from a pile of boulders under a tight dihedral and climb the curving crack, clipping two bolts on the way to a ledge. Work leftward along flakes on chunky rock to the dihedral's start.

Stem up the wild, strenuous dihedral, exit over the roof to the right, then swing back left into a squat leaning corner and the lip anchors.
It is the tougher of the slab problems here: begin right beside the wide crack, which doubles as the descent, and refrain from using it on the way up.
Work up the face's left portion, passing three headwalls separated by two shelves, to reach the anchors just beneath the clifftop.

Start immediately left of Waimea and follow thin edges alongside the crack and the corner up to a pair of anchors by a bulge. Climbers wanting more can carry on through the bulges higher up to a second set of anchors.
